precepts.text: If, delighted with their beauty, they took them to be gods, let them know how much better the Lord of them is, for the first author of beauty hath created them. Real beauty is not the Statue of Liberty; only virgins are beautiful, and God looked at us as beautiful.
precepts.point: I will surely avenge them; my people is led as a flock to the slaughter; I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt, but bring them out with a mighty hand and smite Egypt with plagues as before and destroy all the land thereof. As before means a coming Egypt, the United States. When it comes, we do not want to go down with it.
precepts.why:
Ezra says the Lord will not suffer his people “now to dwell in the land of Egypt”, but will “smite Egypt with plagues, as before”. As before means this is not ancient Egypt; it is a coming Egypt, the United States of America. When it comes, we don't want to go down with it. So why would our people love this Egypt? Because of her beauty.

Wisdom answers: “With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.”

The first author of beauty is our God. Real beauty is not the Statue of Liberty; that is not real beauty. Only virgins are really beautiful. God is the creator of beauty, and he looked at us as beautiful. That is why he refers to us as a woman, as Jeremiah 6:2 shows.

So in this Passover season, get your mind right and remove the leaven. Do not be delighted with the beauty of Egypt and take her for a god. Know how much better the Lord is, who made the beauty.

precepts.why: “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.” God hath shined: going back to that sun, back to that moon. The maker is seen in the beauty of what he made, and out of Zion he has shined.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
See what David’s son says about idols. “But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who call them gods, which are the works of men’s hands”: the nations. “Gold and silver, to shew art in”: the art is the eyes, the ears, the nose, the mouth, the colour, the paints. “And resemblances of beasts”: an idol made like an animal, like a goat.

“Or a stone good for nothing”: you kiss it and it does nothing for you. “The work of an ancient hand”: it has been around since ancient idolatry.

moments.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: God is the first author of beauty and he created us. The standard is his, not the world's.
It is radical because it is totally against what society teaches, and when black people take it on the masses it will cause a revolt.

“Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster.” They started to forget the Creator of those things.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: They deemed “fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars”, or “the lights of heaven”, the sun, the moon and the stars, “to be the gods which govern the world.” But they were not.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them.” And if they were astonished at their power, let them understand “how much mightier he is that made them.”

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “For by the greatness and beauty of the creatures”, the greatness and beauty of the sun and moon we are talking about tonight, “proportionably”, a little bit, “the maker of them is seen.”
What is Christ called? The bridegroom. What is the sun called? The bridegroom. You see a little of him, of his glory, in those things. They represent him.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “But yet for this they are the less to be blamed”: they were seeking God and desirous to find him, and being conversant in his works they searched him diligently and believed their sight, “because the things are beautiful that are seen. Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned.”

They are not pardoned, because they worship the sun and moon as if those are gods themselves, rather than the God that made them. They do not get off on that; the Most High is going to judge them for it regardless.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “For if they were able to know so much, that they could aim at the world; how did they not sooner find out the Lord thereof?” If you were so amazed by the creation, why not go back and honor the Creator?

We learned these things early on, and then we started to worship them. Everybody in this earth searches out what they want to be: to be a doctor you go deep, you search it all out. But when it comes to God, they are confused, ‘I don’t know where God at.’
